svg.title: The passage to a finite transport inventory uses two different reductions. First, a countable family of local leaves with one fixed dictionary key can be summed in that key. Suppose its complex coefficients are ri, its nonnegative leaf bounds are bi, and P i |ri|biescB(S) < ∞, where all leaves have the same support S. Sum the real and imaginary coefficient families separately. Each real sum is a real leaf with bound at most P i |ri|bi; locality, gauge invariance, measurability and its eligibility condition pass to the absolutely convergent sum. The transported quote also passes to the sum by the sound and tuned transport identities. Use charges (1) and i for the two resulting real leaves. They reproduce the original complex family both before transport and in every transported profile, at total marker price at most
